paragraphs.sourceText: The first copyright law in the United States was passed by Congress in 1790. In 1976 Congress enacted the latest copyright law, 26 the technological developments that had occurred since the passage of the Copyright Act of 1909. For example, in 1909, anyone who wanted to make a single copy of a 27 work for personal use had to do so by hand. The very process 28 a limitation on the quantity of materials copied. Today, a photocopier can do the work in seconds: the limitation has disappeared. The 1909 law did not provide full protection for films and sound recordings, nor did it 29 the need to protect radio and television. As a result, 30 of the law and abuses of the intent of the law have lessened the 31 rewards of authors, artists, and producers. The 1976 Copyright Act has not prevented these abuses fully, but it has clarified the legal rights of the injured parties and given them an 32 for remedy.

Since 1976 the Act has been 33 to include computer software, and guidelines have been adopted for fair use of television broadcasts. These changes have cleared up much of the confusion and conflict that followed 34 the 1976 legislation.

The fine points of the law are decided by the courts and by acceptable common practice over time. As these decisions and agreements are made, we modify our behavior accordingly. For now, we need to 35 the law and its guidelines as accurately as we can and to act in a fair manner.

paragraphs.sourceText: Fear can be an effective way to change behavior. One study compared the effects of high-fear and low-fear appeals on changes in attitudes and behaviors related to dental hygiene (卫生）. One group of subjects was shown awful pictures of 36 teeth and diseased gums；another group was shown less frightening materials such as plastic teeth, charts, and graphs. Subjects who saw the frightening materials reported more anxiety and a greater 37 to change the way they took care of their teeth than the low-fear group did.

But were these reactions actually 38 into better dental hygiene practices? To answer this important question, subjects were called back to the laboratory on two 39 (five days and six weeks after the experiment). They chewed disclosing wafers(牙疾诊断片) that give a red stain to any uncleaned areas of the teeth and thus provided a direct 40 of how well they were really taking care of their teeth. The result showed that the high-fear appeal did actually result in greater and more 41 changes in dental hygiene. That is, the subjects 42 to high-fear warnings brushed their teeth more 43 than did those who saw low-fear warnings.

However , to be an effective persuasive device it is very important that the message not be too frightening and that people be given 44 guidelines to help them to reduce the cause of the fear. If this isn’t done, they may reduce their anxiety by denying the message or the 45 of the communicator. If that happens, it is unlikely that either attitude or behavior change will occur. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Street-Level Solution
paragraphs.translationZh: 街道级解决方案

paragraphs.sourceText: A) When I was growing up, one of my father’s favorite sayings (borrowed from the humorist Will Rogers) was：“It isn’t what we don’t know that causes the trouble；it ’ s what we think we know that just isn’t so. One of the main insights to be taken from the 100 000 Homes Campaign and its strategy to end chronic homelessness is that, until recently, our society thought it understood the nature of homelessness, but it didn’t.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 在我成长的过程中，我父亲最喜欢的一句话（借用幽默家威尔·罗杰斯）是：“造成麻烦的不是我们不知道的事情；而是我们自以为知道的事情，但事实并非如此。从十万个家园运动及其结束长期无家可归的战略中得到的主要见解之一是，直到最近，我们的社会还认为它了解无家可归的本质，但事实并非如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) That led to a series of mistaken assumptions about why people become homeless and what they need. Many of the errors in our homelessness policies have stemmed from the conception that the homeless are a homogeneous group. It’s only in the past 15 years that organizations like Common Ground, and others, have taken a street-level view of the problem—distinguishing the “episodically homeless” from the “chronically homeless” in order to understand their needs at an individual level. This is why we can now envisage a different approach—and get better results.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 这导致了对人们为何无家可归以及他们需要什么的一系列错误假设。我们无家可归者政策中的许多错误都源于这样的观念：无家可归者是一个同质群体。直到过去 15 年，Common Ground 等组织才从街头角度看待问题，将“偶尔无家可归者”与“长期无家可归者”区分开来，以便了解他们的个人需求。这就是为什么我们现在可以设想一种不同的方法并获得更好的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Most readers expressed support for the effort, although a number were skeptical, and a few utterly dismissive, about the chances of long-term homeless people adapting well to housing. This is to be expected; it’s hard to imagine what we haven’t yet seen. As Niccolo Machiavelli wrote in The Prince, one of the major obstacles in any effort to advance systemic change is the “incredulity of men，” which is to say that people “do not readily believe in new things until they have had a long experience of them.” Most of us have witnessed homeless people on the streets for decades. Few have seen formerly homeless people after they have been housed successfully. We don’t have reference points for that story. So we generalize from what we know-or think we know.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 大多数读者表示支持这一努力，尽管也有一些读者对长期无家可归者能否很好地适应住房表示怀疑，还有一些人完全不屑一顾。这是可以预料到的；很难想象我们还没有看到什么。正如尼科洛·马基雅维利在《君主论》中所写，任何推动系统性变革的努力的主要障碍之一是“人们的怀疑”，也就是说，人们“在长期体验新事物之前不会轻易相信它们”。几十年来，我们大多数人都目睹过街头无家可归的人。很少有人见过以前无家可归的人在被成功安置后。我们没有那个故事的参考点。因此，我们根据我们所知道的——或者认为我们所知道的——进行概括。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) But that can be misleading, even to experts. When I asked Rosanne Haggerty, founder of Common Ground, which currently operates 2 310 units of supportive housing (with 552 more under construction), what had been her biggest surprise in this work, she replied : “Fifteen years ago, I would not have believed that people who had been so broken and stuck in homelessness could thrive to the degree that they do in our buildings. ’’ And Becky Kanis, the campaign’s director, commented : ‘There is this sense in our minds that someone who’s on the streets is almost in their DNA different from someone who has a house. The campaign is creating a first-hand experience for many people that that is really not the case.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 但这可能会产生误导，甚至对专家来说也是如此。 Common Ground 目前运营着 2,310 套支持性住房（还有 552 套在建），当我问她在这项工作中最大的惊喜是什么时，她回答说：“十五年前，我不会相信那些如此破碎和陷入无家可归的人能够像在我们的建筑中那样茁壮成长。” ” 该活动的负责人贝基·卡尼斯 (Becky Kanis) 评论道：“我们认为，流落街头的人与拥有房子的人几乎从本质上就不同。该活动为许多人创造了一种亲身体验，事实并非如此。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) One of the startling realizations that I had while researching this column is that anybody could become like a homeless person —all it takes is a traumatic (创伤的）brain injury. A bicycle fall, a car accident, a slip on the ice, or if you’re a soldier, a head wound—and your life could become unrecognizable. James O’Connell, a doctor who has been treating the most vulnerable homeless people on the streets of Boston for 25 years, estimates that 40 percent of the long-term homeless people he’s met had such a brain injury. “For many it was a head injury prior to the time they became homeless，” he said. “They became unpredictable. They’d have mood swings, fits of explosive behavior. They couldn’t hold onto their jobs. Drinking made them feel better. They’d end up on the streets.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 在研究本专栏时，我有一个惊人的认识，那就是任何人都可能变得像无家可归者一样——所需要的只是创伤性脑损伤。骑自行车摔倒、车祸、在冰上滑倒，或者如果你是一名士兵，头部受伤——你的生活可能会变得面目全非。詹姆斯·奥康奈尔 (James O’Connell) 是一名医生，25 年来一直在波士顿街头治疗最脆弱的无家可归者，他估计 40% 的人他遇到的长期无家可归的人都遭受过这样的脑损伤，“对于许多人来说，他们在无家可归之前就受到了头部损伤，”他说，“他们变得不可预测。他们会情绪波动，爆发性行为。他们无法保住自己的工作。喝酒让他们感觉好一点。他们最终会流落街头。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Once homeless people return to housing, they’re in a much better position to rebuild their lives. But it’s important to note that housing alone is not enough. As with many complex social problems, when you get through the initial crisis, you have another problem to solve which is no less challenging. But it is a better problem.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 一旦无家可归者返回住房，他们就能更好地重建生活。但值得注意的是，仅住房是不够的。与许多复杂的社会问题一样，当你度过最初的危机时，你还有另一个同样具有挑战性的问题需要解决。但这是一个更好的问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) Over the past decade, O’Connell has seen this happen. spend half my time on the streets or in the hospital and the other half making house calls to people who lived for years on the streets,” he said. “So from a doctor’s point of view it’s a delightful switch, but it’s not as if putting someone in housing is the answer to addressing all of their problems. It’s the first step. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 在过去的十年里，奥康奈尔目睹了这种情况的发生。他说：“我一半的时间都在街上或医院里度过，另一半的时间则上门拜访那些在街头生活多年的人。因此，从医生的角度来看，这是一个令人愉快的转变，但这并不是说让某人住进住房就能解决他们所有的问题。”这是第一步。 ”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) Once in housing, formerly homeless people can become isolated and lonely. If they’ve lived on the streets for years, they may have acquired a certain standing as well as a sense of pride in their survival skills. Now indoors, those aspects of their identity may be stripped away. Many also experience a profound disorientation at the outset. “If you’re homeless for more than six months, you kind of lose your bearings, ”says Haggerty. “Existence becomes not about overcoming homelessness but about finding food, begging, looking for a job to survive another day. The whole process of how you define stability gets reordered. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 一旦入住，以前无家可归的人可能会变得孤立和孤独。如果他们在街头生活多年，他们可能已经获得了一定的地位，并对自己的生存技能感到自豪。现在在室内，他们身份的这些方面可能会被剥夺。许多人一开始也会经历严重的迷失方向。 “如果你无家可归超过六个月，你就会迷失方向，”哈格蒂说。 “存在不再是为了克服无家可归的问题，而是为了寻找食物、乞讨、寻找工作来度过新的一天。定义稳定性的整个过程被重新排序。 ”

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Many need regular, if not continuous, support with mental health problems, addictions and illnesses— and, equally important, assistance in the day-to-day challenges of life, reacquainting with family, building relationships with neighbors, finding enjoyable activities or work, managing finances, and learning how to eat healthy food.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 许多人需要定期（即使不是持续）支持来解决心理健康问题、成瘾和疾病，同样重要的是，需要帮助应对日常生活挑战、重新熟悉家人、与邻居建立关系、寻找愉快的活动或工作、管理财务以及学习如何吃健康食品。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) For some people, the best solution is to live in a communal(集体)residence, with special services. This isn’t available everywhere, however. In Boston, for example, homeless people tend to be scattered in apartments throughout the city.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 对于某些人来说，最好的解决方案是住在提供特殊服务的公共住宅中。然而，这并不是在所有地方都可用。例如，在波士顿，无家可归的人往往分散在整个城市的公寓里。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Common Ground’s large residences in New York offer insight into the possibilities for change when homeless people have a rich array of supports. In addition to more traditional social services, residents also make use of communal gardens, classes in things like cooking, yoga, theatre and photography, and job placement. Last year, 188 formerly homeless tenants in four of Common Ground^ residences, found jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) Common Ground 在纽约的大型住宅让我们深入了解当无家可归者获得丰富的支持时改变的可能性。除了更传统的社会服务外，居民还可以使用公共花园、烹饪、瑜伽、戏剧和摄影等课程以及就业安置。去年，四栋 Common Ground^ 住宅中的 188 名前无家可归租户找到了工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Because the properties have many services and are well-managed, Haggerty has found posthousing problems to be surprisingly rare. In the past 10 years, there have been only a handful of incidents of quarrels between tenants. There is very little graffiti (涂鸦）or vandalism (破坏）. And the turnover is almost negligible. In the Prince George Hotel in New York, which is home to 208 formerly homeless people and 208 low-income tenants, the average length of tenancy is close to seven years. (All residents pay 30 percent of their income for rent；for the formerly homeless, this comes out of their government benefits.) When people move on, it is usually because they’ve found a preferable apartment.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 由于这些房产有很多服务并且管理良好，哈格蒂发现后期住房问题非常罕见。近10年来，租户之间发生争吵的事件屈指可数。涂鸦和破坏行为很少。而且营业额几乎可以忽略不计。在纽约的乔治王子酒店，住着208名无家可归者和208名低收入房客，平均租期接近七年。（所有居民支付收入的30%用于租金；对于以前无家可归者来说，这来自政府福利。）当人们离开时，通常是因为他们找到了住所。最好的公寓。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) “Tenants also want to participate in shaping the public areas of the buildings，” said Haggerty. “They formed a gardening committee. They want a terrace on the roof. Those are things I didn’t count on.’’ The most common tenant demand? People always want more storage space—but that’s true of every New Yorker,” she adds. “In many ways, we’re a lot like a normal apartment building. Our tenants look like anyone else. ”
paragraphs.translationZh: M）“租户也希望参与塑造建筑物的公共区域，”哈格蒂说。 “他们成立了一个园艺委员会。他们想要在屋顶上有一个露台。这些都是我没想到的。”最常见的租户需求是什么？人们总是想要更多的存储空间，但这对每个纽约人来说都是如此，”她补充道。 “在很多方面，我们很像普通的公寓楼。我们的租户看起来和其他人一样。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) As I mentioned, homelessness is a catch-all for a variety of problems. A number of readers asked whether the campaign will address family homelessness, which has different causes and requires a different solution. I’ve been following some of the promising ideas emerging to address and prevent family homelessness. Later in 2011, I’ll explore these ideas in a column. For now, I’ll conclude with an update on the 100 000 Homes Campaign. Since Tuesday, New Orleans and a few other communities have reported new results. The current count of people housed is 7 043.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 正如我所提到的，无家可归是各种问题的总称。许多读者询问该活动是否会解决家庭无家可归问题，家庭无家可归有不同的原因，需要不同的解决方案。我一直在关注一些解决和防止家庭无家可归问题的有前途的想法。 2011 年晚些时候，我将在专栏中探讨这些想法。现在，我将介绍 100 000 套住房活动的最新情况。自周二以来，新奥尔良和其他一些社区报告了新的结果。目前收容人数为 7 043 人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Tenants in Common Ground’s residences all want more room for storage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. Common Ground 住宅的租户都希望有更多的存储空间。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Homes Campaign provides first-hand proof that the homeless are not what they were once believed to be.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 家园运动提供了第一手证据，证明无家可归者并不像他们曾经认为的那样。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Common Ground’s residences are well-managed and by and large peaceful.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. Common Ground 的住宅管理良好，总体上很安静。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. Housing the homeless is only the first step to solving all their problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 为无家可归者提供住房只是解决他们所有问题的第一步。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. A large percent of the chronically homeless have suffered from brain injury.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 很大一部分长期无家可归者患有脑损伤。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. After being housed many homeless people become confused at first as to how to deal with life off the street.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 许多无家可归者在获得安置后，起初对如何应对街头生活感到困惑。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. Some people think the best way to help the homeless is to provide them with communal housing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 有些人认为帮助无家可归者的最佳方式是为他们提供公共住房。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. The homeless with health problems should be given regular support in their daily lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 有健康问题的无家可归者应在日常生活中得到定期支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. Until recently American society has failed to see what homelessness is all about.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 直到最近，美国社会还没有明白无家可归到底意味着什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. Many formerly homeless tenants in New York’s Common Ground’s residences got hired.
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 纽约 Common Ground 住宅区的许多以前无家可归的租户都被雇用了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Technology can make us smarter or stupider, and we need to develop a set of principles to guide our everyday behavior and make sure that tech is improving and not hindering our mental processes. One of the big questions being debated today is: What kind of information do we need to have stored in our heads, and what kind can we leave “in the cloud，” to be accessed as necessary?
paragraphs.translationZh: 技术可以让我们变得更聪明或更愚蠢，我们需要制定一套原则来指导我们的日常行为，并确保技术正在改进而不是阻碍我们的思维过程。今天争论的重大问题之一是：我们需要将什么样的信息存储在我们的头脑中，以及我们可以将什么样的信息留在“云端”以便在必要时访问？

paragraphs.sourceText: An increasingly powerful group within education are championing “digital literacy”. In their view, skills beat knowledge, developing “digital literacy” is more important than learning mere content, and all facts are now Google-able and therefore unworthy of committing to memory. But even the most sophisticated digital literacy skills won’t help students and workers navigate the world if they don’t have a broad base of knowledge about how the world actually operates. If you focus on the delivery mechanism and not the content, you’re doing kids a disservice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 教育界一个日益强大的群体正在倡导“数字素养”。在他们看来，技能胜过知识，发展“数字素养”比学习单纯的内容更重要，所有事实现在都可以通过谷歌搜索，因此不值得牢记在心。但如果学生和工人没有关于世界实际运作方式的广泛知识基础，那么即使是最复杂的数字素养技能也无法帮助学生和工人驾驭世界。如果你专注于传递机制而不是内容，那么你就是在伤害孩子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Indeed, evidence from cognitive science challenges the notion that skills can exist independent of factual knowledge. Data from the last thirty years leads to a conclusion that is not scientifically challengeable：thinking well requires knowing facts, and that’s true not only because you need something to think about. The very processes that teachers care about most —critical thinking processes—are intimately intertwined(交织）with factual knowledge that is stored in long-term memory.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，认知科学的证据挑战了技能可以独立于事实知识而存在的观念。过去三十年的数据得出了一个在科学上不具有挑战性的结论：良好的思考需要了解事实，这不仅是因为你需要思考一些东西。教师最关心的过程——批判性思维过程——与存储在长期记忆中的事实知识紧密地交织在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: In other words, just because you can Google the date of Black Tuesday doesn’t mean you understand why the Great Depression happened or how it compares to our recent economic slump. There is no doubt that the students of today, and the workers of tomorrow, will need to innovate, collaborate and evaluate. But such skills can’t be separated from the knowledge that gives rise to them. To innovate, you have to know what came before. To collaborate, you have to contribute knowledge to the joint venture. And to evaluate, you have to compare new information against knowledge you’ve already mastered.
paragraphs.translationZh: 换句话说，仅仅因为你可以在谷歌上搜索黑色星期二的日期，并不意味着你了解大萧条为什么会发生，或者它与我们最近的经济衰退相比如何。毫无疑问，今天的学生和明天的工人都需要创新、协作和评估。但这些技能不能与产生它们的知识分开。为了创新，你必须知道之前发生了什么。要进行合作，您必须为合资企业贡献知识。为了进行评估，您必须将新信息与您已经掌握的知识进行比较。

paragraphs.sourceText: So here’s a principle for thinking in a digital world, in two parts. First, acquire a base of factual knowledge in any domain in which you want to perform well. This base supplies the essential foundation for building skills, and it can’t be outsourced (外包） to a search engine.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这是数字世界的思考原则，分为两部分。首先，在您想要表现出色的任何领域获取事实知识基础。这个基础为培养技能提供了必要的基础，并且它不能外包给搜索引擎。

paragraphs.sourceText: Second, take advantage of computers’ invariable memory, but also the brain’s elaborative memory. Computers are great when you want to store information that shouldn’t change. But brains are the superior choice when you want information to change, in interesting and useful ways：to connect up with other facts and ideas, to acquire successive layers of meaning, to steep for a while in your accumulated knowledge and experience and so produce a richer mental brew. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 其次，利用计算机的不变记忆以及大脑的精细记忆。当您想要存储不应更改的信息时，计算机非常有用。但是，当你希望信息以有趣且有用的方式发生变化时，大脑是更好的选择：与其他事实和想法联系起来，获得连续的多层意义，暂时沉浸在你积累的知识和经验中，从而产生更丰富的精神酝酿。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: America’s recent history has been a persistent tilt to the West—of people, ideas, commerce and even political power. California and Texas are the twin poles of the West, but very different ones. For most of the 20th century the home of Silicon Valley and Hollywood has been the brainier and trendier of the two. Texas has trailed behind：its stereotype has been a conservative Christian in cowboy boots. But twins can change places. Is that happening now?
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国近代历史在人员、思想、商业甚至政治权力方面一直向西方倾斜。加利福尼亚州和德克萨斯州是西部的双极，但又截然不同。在 20 世纪的大部分时间里，硅谷和好莱坞是两者中更聪明、更时尚的故乡。德克萨斯州落后了：它的刻板印象是穿着牛仔靴的保守基督徒。但双胞胎可以改变位置。现在有这种情况吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: It is easy to find evidence that California is in a panic. At the start of this month the once golden state started paying creditors in IOUs (欠条).The gap between projected outgoings and income for the current fiscal (财政的）year has leapt to a horrible $26 billion. With no sign of a new budget to close this gulf, one credit agency has already downgraded California’s debt. As budgets are cut, universities will let in fewer students, prisoners will be released early and schemes to protect the vulnerable will be rolled back.
paragraphs.translationZh: 很容易找到证据表明加州陷入恐慌。本月初，这个曾经的金州开始向债权人支付欠条。当前财政年度的预计支出和收入之间的差距已跃升至可怕的 260 亿美元。由于没有新预算来弥合这一鸿沟，一家信贷机构已经下调了加州的债务评级。随着预算的削减，大学将招收更少的学生，囚犯将提前获释，保护弱势群体的计划将被撤销。

paragraphs.sourceText: By contrast, Texas has coped well with the recession, with an unemployment rate two points below the national average and one of the lowest rates of housing repossession. In part this is because Texan banks, hard hit in the last property bust, did not overexpand this time. Texas also clearly offers a different model, based on small government. It has no state capital-gains or income tax, and a business- friendly and immigrant-tolerant attitude. It is home to more Fortune 500 companies than any other state.
paragraphs.translationZh: 相比之下，德克萨斯州很好地应对了经济衰退，失业率比全国平均水平低两个百分点，也是住房收回率最低的州之一。部分原因是，在上次房地产泡沫破裂中遭受重创的德克萨斯州银行这次没有过度扩张。德克萨斯州还显然提供了一种基于小政府的不同模式。它没有国家资本利得税或所得税，并且采取对商业友好和移民宽容的态度。它是财富 500 强公司的所在地，比任何其他州都多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Despite all this, it still seems too early to hand over America’s future to Texas. To begin with, that lean Texan model has its own problems. It has not invested enough in education, and many experts rightly worry about a “lost generation” of mostly Hispanic Texans with insufficient skills for the demands of the knowledge economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管如此，将美国的未来交给德克萨斯州似乎还为时过早。首先，精益的德克萨斯模式有其自身的问题。它在教育方面的投资不够，许多专家担心“迷失的一代”（主要是西班牙裔德克萨斯人）缺乏满足知识经济需求的技能。

paragraphs.sourceText: Second, it has never paid to bet against a state with as many inventive people as California. Even if Hollywood has gone into depression, it still boasts an unequalled array of sunrise industries and the most brisk venture-capital industry on the planet. The state also has an awesome ability to reinvent itself —as it did when its defence industry collapsed at the end of the cold war.
paragraphs.translationZh: 其次，做空加州这样一个拥有如此多创新人才的州从来没有得到过回报。即使好莱坞已经陷入萧条，它仍然拥有一系列无与伦比的朝阳产业和地球上最活跃的风险投资产业。该国还拥有强大的自我重塑能力——就像冷战结束时其国防工业崩溃时那样。

paragraphs.sourceText: The truth is that both states could learn from each other. Texas still lacks California’s great universities and lags in terms of culture. California could adopt not just Texas’s leaner state, but also its more bipartisan (两党的）approach to politics. There is no perfect model of government: it is America’s genius to have 50 public-policy laboratories competing to find out what works best. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实是，两国可以互相学习。德克萨斯州仍然缺乏加州的优秀大学，并且在文化方面落后。加州不仅可以采用德克萨斯州更精简的州，还可以采用更加两党合作的政治方式。不存在完美的政府模式：美国的天才在于拥有 50 个公共政策实验室，竞相寻找最有效的方案。
